The petitioner filed an application under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) in the Court of Munsif 3rd Court, Comilla for preemption alleging, inter alia, that the opposite party was a stranger purchaser in respect of the land in question while the petitioner was a co-sharer tenant of the holding. The said miscellaneous case was allowed exparte on 7.3.75. Thereupon the opposite-party filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the exparte order on 15.5.75 alleging, besides other things, non-service and fraudulent suppression of notice of the preemption case. 

 12. In so far as the submission of Mr. Haque the learned Advocate, to the fact that the exparte order passed in the application under Order 9 rule 13 should be treated as decree, is concerned, it may be pointed out that Ibrahim, J. in the aforesaid decision negatived the said contention by analysing the scheme of section 26F of the Bengal Tenancy Act. The reasoning given therein is equally applicable to an order passed under section 96 of the Act. 13. We would like to add yet another reason as to the difficulty in construing an order under section 96 of the Act to be a decree. In that case, His Lordship refused to interfere with the appellate order setting aside and dismissing the execution case itself upon grounds beyond the scope of Order 21 rule 90 C.P.C. out of which the appeal arose, on consideration that by reason of the provisions of section 35, sub-clause (iii) of the Bengal Agricultural Debtors Act, the award was still subsisting and the decree was null and void and as such the execution thereof did not lie and setting aside of the appellate order which was passed in excess of jurisdiction would amount to restoring a patently illegal proceeding.
